absorption_notes: Absorbed as a fat-soluble retinoid with dietary fat; 70-90% at usual doses
notes: The form that carries the teratogenicity and hepatotoxicity risk. A multivitamin should keep preformed retinol moderate.

absorption_notes: About 15.6% bioavailable from plant foods; conversion to retinol is regulated and inefficient
notes: No UL, but 20-30 mg/day increased lung cancer risk in smokers. A 'vegetarian' multi may use it as its only vitamin A, which makes the label amount misleading.

absorption_notes: Competitive absorption; fat required
notes: Includes lutein, lycopene and alpha-carotene. Useful for eye health at AREDS2 doses, not a substitute for retinol in deficiency.

absorption_notes: Raises 25(OH)D more than D2 at the same dose; absorbed with fat
notes: The preferred form. 1,000 IU = 25 mcg. Most multis supply 400-1,000 IU; 2,000 IU is common in premium products.

absorption_notes: Raises total 25(OH)D less than D3 and can lower 25(OH)D3
notes: Acceptable but inferior. Used in some vegan and prescription products.

absorption_notes: Requires fat and bile; about twice the activity of synthetic per mg
notes: Labels in mg alpha-tocopherol already normalise for potency.

absorption_notes: Ester must be hydrolysed; only 4 of 8 stereoisomers retained
notes: Not 'fake', just less potent per mg. The ester is stable, which is why tablets use it.

absorption_notes: Gamma-tocopherol has different chemistry and may complement alpha
notes: Most evidence is for alpha-tocopherol alone. Mixed tocopherols are a reasonable formulation choice, not a proven advantage.

absorption_notes: Requires fat; absorbed with chylomicrons
notes: The main dietary K. Warfarin patients need stable intake, not avoidance.

absorption_notes: Short half-life; large doses used in Japan for osteoporosis
notes: No fracture benefit established in Western trials at multivitamin doses.

absorption_notes: Long half-life (about 3 days); accumulates
notes: Popular in premium multis. No outcome trial shows benefit from adding it to a multivitamin.

absorption_notes: Saturable absorption; 200 mg doses absorb almost completely
notes: Above 1 g, absorption falls and GI effects rise.

absorption_notes: Same ascorbate anion; gentler on the stomach
notes: Useful for people with reflux; otherwise equivalent.

absorption_notes: Ascorbate with flavonoids; no consistent advantage
notes: Human steady-state studies find no difference from synthetic ascorbic acid.

absorption_notes: Active transport at low doses; passive at high doses
notes: Deficiency is rare outside alcohol use disorder and bariatric surgery.

absorption_notes: Converted to thiamin; higher tissue levels in some studies
notes: Used for diabetic neuropathy; not a standard multivitamin ingredient.

absorption_notes: Saturable; excess excreted (bright yellow urine)
notes: R5P is the active coenzyme form but is hydrolysed before absorption.

absorption_notes: Flushes via prostaglandin release
notes: Above 35 mg causes flushing; gram doses are hepatotoxic. The UL applies to synthetic niacin.

absorption_notes: No flushing; different hepatic handling
notes: Better tolerated, but still above the UL in high-potency multis. Hepatotoxicity is rare below 1 g.

absorption_notes: CoA precursor; widespread in food
notes: Deficiency is essentially unknown in people eating a mixed diet.

absorption_notes: Passive absorption; excess excreted
notes: Above 100 mg/day causes sensory neuropathy; cases reported at lower doses with long use.

absorption_notes: Dephosphorylated before absorption then rephosphorylated
notes: The active form; no proven clinical advantage at multivitamin doses.

absorption_notes: 85% bioavailable; requires DHFR and MTHFR conversion
notes: Stable and cheap. Unmetabolised folic acid appears in plasma at doses above about 200-400 mcg.

absorption_notes: Already reduced; raises plasma folate at least as much as folic acid
notes: Preferred by some clinicians, especially in MTHFR TT. No outcome trial shows superiority. Glucosamine salt is common.

absorption_notes: Intermediate in the folate pathway
notes: Used in some high-end products; little comparative human data.

absorption_notes: Requires intrinsic factor or passive absorption at high doses; stable
notes: The standard, cheap, effective form. Supplies cyanide at microgram doses, which is not clinically relevant.

absorption_notes: Converted to the same intracellular pools; light-sensitive
notes: Marketed as 'active'. No consistent clinical advantage over cyanocobalamin.

absorption_notes: Converted intracellularly
notes: No advantage demonstrated in oral supplements.

absorption_notes: Widely distributed; deficiency rare
notes: High doses interfere with streptavidin-biotin immunoassays for TSH and troponin.

absorption_notes: Converted to acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine; TMAO produced by gut bacteria
notes: Most multis contain little or no choline; 25 mg is trivial against a 550 mg AI.

absorption_notes: Requires gastric acid; absorption falls without food or with PPIs
notes: Compact and cheap; the usual multivitamin form.

absorption_notes: Absorbed without acid; can be taken fasting
notes: Better for older adults and PPI users. A multivitamin dose is far below trial doses for fracture prevention.

absorption_notes: Best absorbed fasting but poorly tolerated; vitamin C increases absorption
notes: The reference form for treating deficiency. In a multivitamin it is mainly a GI irritant for people who do not need it.

absorption_notes: Stable in the gut; fewer GI effects at equal efficacy
notes: Increasingly used in prenatal and women's multis. Still iron, still requires a reason.

absorption_notes: Slow release; lower toxicity in overdose
notes: Safer in overdose, which matters in households with children, but not common in multis.

absorption_notes: About 4% absorbed versus 9-11% for soluble salts; also a laxative
notes: The default in cheap multis because it is compact. Contributes some magnesium, less than the label implies.

absorption_notes: Well absorbed; osmotic laxative at higher doses
notes: Good general-purpose form. Diarrhoea limits dose.

absorption_notes: Gentle on the gut; absorption equal to oxide in the only direct trial
notes: Worth a premium for tolerability, not proven better absorption.

absorption_notes: Well absorbed; malate may be less laxative
notes: Used in 'energy' multis without evidence of an energy effect.

absorption_notes: Needs acid; cheap and compact
notes: Fine at 10-15 mg; poor choice for therapeutic zinc doses.

absorption_notes: Well absorbed with or without food
notes: Common in premium multis.

absorption_notes: Gentle; less competition from iron and calcium
notes: Good tolerability. Still counts toward the 40 mg UL.

absorption_notes: Well absorbed; popular in standalone supplements
notes: No clear advantage over citrate or bisglycinate.

absorption_notes: Incorporated into body proteins; long tissue half-life
notes: The preferred form. 200 mcg is 50% of the UL.

absorption_notes: Not incorporated into proteins; excreted faster
notes: Effective for correcting deficiency; less tissue retention.

absorption_notes: Variable composition; mixture of species
notes: Content varies by lot, which is a quality-control problem.

absorption_notes: Complete absorption; thyroid autoregulates
notes: 150 mcg covers the RDA. Kelp can vary widely and overshoot.

absorption_notes: Highly variable iodine content
notes: A classic source of unintended excess. Avoid unquantified kelp.

absorption_notes: Competes with zinc and iron
notes: Needed when zinc is high. 0.9-1 mg is a sensible match for 15-25 mg zinc.

absorption_notes: Absorption low; competition with other minerals
notes: No UL, and no reliable evidence for glycaemic benefit in people without deficiency.

absorption_notes: Competes with iron
notes: UL 11 mg. Several multis supply 2-4 mg, which is unnecessary but below the UL.

absorption_notes: Readily absorbed
notes: Deficiency is essentially unknown outside parenteral nutrition.

absorption_notes: Rapid absorption; excreted renally
notes: Small human trials suggest effects on sex hormones and calcium, but no outcome data.

absorption_notes: Concentrate in the macula; fat required
notes: AREDS2 used 10 mg lutein + 2 mg zeaxanthin. Standard multis contain token amounts (140-300 mcg).

absorption_notes: Poor and variable absorption; food and lipid formulations help
notes: No outcome evidence at multivitamin doses; adds cost.
